newsitem.title: USA: Japan attitude on biotech mixed - US ag counselor.
newsitem.headline: Japan attitude on biotech mixed - US ag counselor.

text.p: The Japanese government and scientific community see the possibilities of biotech crops to bolster their agriculture sector but consumers have concerns, a U.S. Agriculture Department official said Wednesday.
"At the official level and the scientific level it's not only acceptance but actually I would say even enthusiasm for biotech products," said John Childs, USDA ag counselor in Tokyo.
But he said Japanese consumers do not understand the technology and "have some concerns, however vaguely expressed."
"We're at a stage now where I think it's a good time to sort of educate the Japanese consumers about what GMOs (genetically modified organisms) are all about."
He said the U.S. had been working for two years to cultivate understanding, especially with the Japanese government.
The Clinton Administration has embraced genetically engineered crops as vital to feeding a hungry world. U.S. farmers have been planting them in greater numbers because of their higher yields.

The U.S. has clashed with the European Union over EU rules that call for labeling of foods made with biotech crops and demands by some EU activists that biotech crops be handled, stored and sold separately from other crops.
